ambient_events: The grinder runs for four seconds somewhere behind the counter, and stops.
Far below, a tram crosses the junction without making any sound at all.
Steam sighs off the wand, and the smell of it reaches the far boards.
A page turns in one of the deep chairs by the glass, unhurried.
Light slides the length of the room as something with landing lamps banks out over the district.
description: A coffee house on the eighteenth floor, which is a thing only a building like this can afford to be. The east wall is glass from carpet to ceiling, and Coldwater lies out beyond it entire: the rail yards stitched in sodium, the Marquee signs working through their cycles, the whole basin going blue toward the Curtain. Inside is figured walnut and a short marble counter with a brass espresso rig standing on it, polished to the point of vanity. Deep leather chairs face each other across boards inlaid into the tables themselves, ebony and holly, worn pale at the centre files. The carpet takes every footfall. Nobody hurries in this room, and nobody who drinks here has ever had to. Step in to the elevator.

window.description: The east wall is one unbroken sheet of glass, black-framed at the floor and the ceiling and nowhere in between. Eighteen floors of Coldwater hang in it, close enough to pick out a lit stairwell, high enough that none of it makes a sound.
window.name: the east glass

name: Bishop's Blend
